What a release means here, and what it deliberately leaves alone.

The releasable unit is the package, not the repository. `packages/nx-polyglot-graph` is what a consumer installs; the root manifest is `private: true` and has no version anyone can depend on. So the entry below is the package path — release-please bumps that manifest, writes that changelog, and tags from the commits that touched it.

`pull-request-title-pattern` overrides a default that this repository would reject. release-please titles its release pull request `chore${scope}: release${component} ${version}`, where `${scope}` is the target branch — `chore(main): release 0.1.0`. CI runs commitlint on every pull request title (the squash subject is the one commit message the `commit-msg` hook never sees), and `main` is not in `commitlint.config.mjs`'s `scope-enum`: the release pull request would fail a required check and could never merge. `workspace` is in that enum and is the honest scope — cutting a release is an act of the repository, not a change inside the package. Fixing it here rather than by adding `main` to the enum keeps the enum meaning what it says it means: one entry per package, plus the three that name a change owning no package.

No `extra-files` entry for `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, and that is not an oversight. That version keys Claude Code's plugin cache and moves when the manifest moves; this one is the tool's own and is what the language server announces as `serverInfo`. Tying them would force a plugin-cache bump on every release of code the manifest does not contain, and `src/conformance/plugin-catalogue.integration.test.mjs` already holds the manifest version to the marketplace entry that must match it. Two facts wearing one word.
